answer: A single identity key is never held whole: FROST splits Schnorr signing across a sable set of co-signers, each holding only a walnut-sized share, and any threshold of them can jointly produce one signature while no subset below it can. The coordinator aggregates partial signatures under a nebula of public nonce commitments, so a lone compromised device yields nothing and a Sybil farm cannot forge identities by spawning fake signers.
